FootballSeptember 05, 2026

Hawkeyes Down Northern Illinois to Open Season

The 22nd-ranked University of Iowa football team defeated Northern Illinois, 40-0, in its season opener on Saturday afternoon at Kinnick Stadium.

Opens in a new window Box Score (PDF) Opens in a new window Postgame News Conference Transcript (PDF)
Share
TwitterFacebookEmail
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:13
Instaread

IOWA CITY, Iowa — The 22nd-ranked University of Iowa football team defeated Northern Illinois, 40-0, in its season opener on Saturday afternoon at Kinnick Stadium. 

The Hawkeyes racked up 507 yards of total offense while holding Northern Illinois to 120.

Kamari Moulton led the Hawkeyes on the ground, rushing for 183 yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries. At quarterback, Hank Brown completed 12 of 20 passes for 129 yards and a touchdown, while Jeremy Hecklinski completed 7 of 16 attempts for 76 yards and a touchdown. Jimmy Sullivan closed out the game, going 2-for-4 for 13 yards.

Tony Diaz and DJ Vonnahme paced the receiving corps. Diaz caught seven passes for 84 yards and a touchdown, while Vonnahme hauled in four receptions for 42 yards.

Defensively, Cam Buffington led Iowa with six tackles. The Hawkeyes limited the Huskies to 120 yards of total offense and recorded six sacks, including 1.5 by Joseph Anderson and one each from Julian Manson and Chima Chineke. Deshaun Lee added an interception, while Ty Hudkins recovered a fumble.

Special teams also contributed heavily. Caden Buhr converted field goals from 45 and 34 yards, and Evan James returned a third-quarter punt 77 yards for a touchdown.

QUOTING KIRK FERENTZ

"Just, you know, to start out, just really pleased and proud of the team. Pleased about the outcome and then certainly proud of the team. I think they really did a good job today. They showed up, played hard, they competed and they handled the heat. It was pretty intense out there, just like you guys had to deal with it as well.

But the bigger picture, I thought they did a good job with the preparation all week, and that showed up today. And we had heat to deal with all week, too. It wasn't so good on Tuesday, but they bounced back, came back Wednesday and put a good day out there, and I think that showed up today. So happy about that.

Obviously, good to get the win. Every game, that's the goal. We don't talk a lot about it, but why would you put the work in if you're not trying to do that? And it's just really an overall very positive first step for us, considering our team right now, the makeup of our team.

So really, I think for me going into it, the biggest curiosity and biggest interest was just how the new guys were going to handle things. And you look at our four captains, all are guys that have experience that, you know, feel pretty good about. We know what they're going to do, how they're going to show up, know they're giving leadership and doing things right. But boy, we had a lot of guys that really haven't been out there in conditions where they're starting and being counted on to be a productive force.

I thought that was a really positive thing, and that's basically all three phases: offense, defense, special teams. A lot of new faces, some a little bit more prominent than others. So thought that was a really positive thing.

I thought both quarterbacks were productive. It was a good first start for both of them. And like I said earlier, whatever they've done prior to this really, in my mind, doesn't count. That's all erased from the memory bank. It's what they're going to do this season with our team. And I thought both of them did some good things, so really pleased for both of those guys.

And then just, you know, think about offensively, I think our overall execution for a first game was pretty decent. And I'll make special mention for Kamari. He just looked faster, quicker, more confident than I've seen him. And he's an experienced football player, one of the guys we're definitely counting on, but I thought he really looked good. That's the best we've seen him. So that's part of maturity and development, I think, and really good to see that.

Then defensively, where we've got a lot of new faces, I thought they responded really well today, too. Played hard, you know, didn't have any major issues until we got in that fourth quarter. We had a few things that were a little bit interesting. But for the most part, guys were doing what they were supposed to do and doing it pretty hard. Happy about that.

And then on special teams, had a few bumps early. Missed an opportunity on a plus-50 punt, missed a field goal. Yeah, that was kind of a bad sequence in there. We missed the thing, but Deshaun got the pick, and then couldn't do anything with that field position, which was kind of disappointing, not to get any points out of it.

But, you know, a lot of good things there, too. I thought our kickoff coverage was excellent, and it was good to see the specialists. Boston did a good job with the punting, I thought, for the most part there. The plus-50 one was a close miss.

A lot of positives there, but the guys were playing hard and they were going hard. So feel good about that. And just again, good to get off to a positive start. Happy about that.

And then last, just want to thank the fans. If it's hot on the field, it's hotter in the stands, I know that. And so really give them credit for, A, showing up, and then B, supporting us throughout the game. It's always good to be on the field. And again, all these new guys are going to figure that out, that it's a pretty good environment down there."

PHOTOS

HOW IT HAPPENED 

  • Iowa capped a 10-play, 75-yard opening drive with a 6-yard touchdown pass from Hank Brown to Tony Diaz at the 9:52 mark of the first quarter.
  • On the next drive, Moulton burst free for a 50-yard touchdown run to increase the lead with 6:46 left in the first.
  • Moulton struck again less than three minutes later, capping a four-play, 70-yard drive with a 37-yard touchdown rush with 4:10 remaining in the opening period.
  • In the second quarter, Jeremy Hecklinski connected with Xavier Williams on an 8-yard touchdown pass with 7:40 left in the half.
  • Caden Buhr drilled a 45-yard field goal with 3:34 remaining in the second quarter before adding a 34-yard field goal with two seconds left in the first half.
  • With 2:20 left in the third quarter, James broke loose for a 77-yard punt return touchdown.

POSTGAME NOTES

  • The Hawkeyes have won 11 of their last 13 season openers since 2014 and are now 23-4 in openers under head coach Kirk Ferentz.
  • The shutout is the 19th under Ferentz and it is the second season-opening shutout in the last three seasons.
  • Iowa’s 40 points are the most scored in an opener since 2024. The team’s 33 first-half points were the most in the first-half of a season opener since 2005 (49 points vs. Ball State).

INDIVIDUAL NOTES

    • Fourth-year quarterback Hank Brown completed 12-of-20 attempts for 129 yards and one touchdown, while third-year quarterback Jeremy Hecklinski was 7-of-16 for 76 yards and one touchdown.
      • Brown led the offense on three touchdown drives on his first three possessions. Iowa scored 27 points and had 283 yards in five offensive series.
      • Hecklinski guided the unit to seven points, 154 yards and one touchdown on five series.
    • Fourth-year Kamari Moulton recorded his second career 100-yard game, finishing with 11 carries for a career-high 183 yards and two touchdowns.
      • Moulton had a 50-yard touchdown run – the second-longest rush of his career – and a 37-yard score in the first quarter. He had 132 yards in the opening quarter alone, surpassing his previous career best (118 at Maryland, 2024).
      • Moulton’s 183 yards are the most for a Hawkeye in a season opener since Tavian Banks (203 yards) in 1997 and the most in a game since Kaleb Johnson (at Minnesota) in 2024.
      • Moulton scored two touchdowns for the third time in his career.
    • Third-year WR Tony Diaz had seven catches for 84 yards with one touchdown.
      • Diaz had three receptions for 32 yards (and drew a pass interference penalty in the end zone) on Iowa’s opening possession of the season, which culminated with a 6-yard touchdown reception.
      • His 84 yards are the most by a Hawkeye wide receiver since Jacob Gill’s 138 yards at UCLA in 2024.
      • His seven receptions are the most by an Iowa wideout since Kaleb Brown had seven against Illinois in 2023.
    • Third-year RB Xavier Williams had an 8-yard touchdown reception on a screen in the second quarter, making the score 27-0. It was his first career receiving touchdown (fourth overall TD).
    • Second-year WR Evan James had a 77-yard punt return for a touchdown in the third quarter. It is the 15th longest punt return for a score in program history.
      • Iowa has had a punt return for a touchdown in each of the past four seasons.
    • Fifth-year DB Deshaun Lee had his fourth career interception in the second quarter and he returned the pick 17 yards to the NIU 45.
    • Fourth-year DL Brice Stevenson forced a fumble and third-year Ty Hudkins recovered in the fourth quarter. They were the first of both of their careers.
    • Kicker Caden Buhr finished 2-of-3 on field goal attempts, connecting from 45 and 34 yards. They were the first attempts of his collegiate career.

MISCELLANIOUS

  • Iowa finished with 507 yards of total offense in the game.
    • The Hawkeyes had 251 yards in the first quarter and 372 yards in the first half. The 372 yards are the most in an opening half since 2019 vs. Middle Tennessee State (358).
  • The Hawkeyes have scored 40, 34 and 40 points in offensive coordinator Tim Lester’s first three seasons with the program.
    • Iowa's 507 yards of total offense are the most in a game under Lester.
  • The total offense is the most in a season opener since finishing with 593 (2002).
  • It was the most yards by a Hawkeye offense since 2019 against Middle Tennessee (644).
  • Iowa's defense limited the Huskies to 120 yards of total offense and seven first downs. The 120 yards are tied for the sixth-fewest allowed in a game during the Kirk Ferentz era, while the seven first downs are tied for the seventh-fewest allowed.
    • NIU had 22 yards in the first quarter and 24 in the first half. The Huskies didn’t pick up their initial first down until the 4:10 mark in the third quarter (and it came via penalty).
  • Iowa's 289 rushing yards are its most in a game since rushing for 310 yards against Albany in 2025.
    • Iowa has rushed for 200 or more yards in 13 games under Lester.
  • Iowa forced two turnovers and won the turnover battle, 2-1.
    • The Hawkeyes are 76-5 when winning the turnover battle since 2012.
  • Eleven Hawkeyes – Leighton Jones (OL), Cael Winter (OL), Jack Dotzler (OL), Tony Diaz (WR), Hank Brown (QB), Cam Buffington (LB), Jacob Wallace (DB), Anthony Hawkins (DB), Kenneth Merriweather (DL), Will Hubert (DL) and Iose Epenesa (DL) – made their first career starts at Iowa.
  • The 90-degree temperature at kickoff is the tied for the fourth-hottest home game in program history.
  • Iowa won the toss and elected to receive. The Hawkeyes have played 342 games under head coach Kirk Ferentz. Iowa has opened the game on offense 251 times (162-89). The Hawkeyes have opened the game on defense 91 times (52-39).

UP NEXT

The Hawkeyes return to action next week, hosting Iowa State in the Iowa Corn Cy-Hawk Series on Sept. 12 at 6:30 p.m. (CT).
